output.llm_reasoning: The zwitterionic adduct has an ammonium N8+ and an amidate N5- on the same urea carbon. One proton transfer from N8 to N5 gives the neutral urea target. The current state contains no separate acid or base to act as a shuttle; the amine was consumed 1:1. The transfer is therefore drawn as an intramolecular N8-H to N5 proton shift. In practice it is likely assisted by another adduct or amine molecule. The N5 lone pair takes the proton, and the N8-H electrons stay on N8, which neutralizes both centers.
